target.//fingerprints: EVERY certificate either lane may be signed by, under the one applicationId (D3(a)). Omitting one breaks App Links for every user of that lane, silently. The Play side is a LIST and never a single value: the current app signing key has a classical certificate AND, under quantum-ready signing, a post-quantum one, and Google can ROTATE the key, which adds a Previous entry that installs already in the field still verify against. Read them all at Play Console -> Setup -> App integrity -> App signing, from the key panels. The direct APK is signed by K10 (`apksigner verify --print-certs xchain-wallet-vX.Y.Z.apk`), which is not on Google's page at all.
target.//do-not-paste-googles-snippet: That page ends with a `Digital Asset Links JSON` block captioned 'copy and paste this snippet into your Digital Asset Links JSON file'. Do not. Measured 2026-08-07, it offered ONE fingerprint and it was the key Google had already rotated AWAY from, so pasting it drops both live Play certificates and K10 at once. Listing a superseded certificate is harmless (it only widens what Android accepts); omitting a live one is the silent, cached failure. The generator refuses any build that publishes fewer fingerprints than the live file already carries.
